scores.answer: Given your program end date of May 15, 2026, you may properly file your Form I-765 for post-completion OPT no later than 2026-06-14 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(B)(2)].

You must file Form I-765 for post-completion OPT from 2026-02-14 to 2026-05-31 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(B)(2)]. This filing must occur no later than 30 days after the program end date and within 30 days of the DSO recommendation [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(B)(2)].
You have 61 days of unemployment left on your post-completion OPT [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E)]. Out of the 90 allowed days of unemployment, 29 have been used [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E)].

You can file Form I-765 for the 24-month STEM OPT extension from 2027-03-02 to 2027-05-31 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(C)]. You may request this extension by filing the form up to 90 days prior to the expiration date of your current OPT employment authorization [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(C)].

Your STEM OPT validation reports are due to the DSO on the following dates: validation report 1 is due by 2027-12-15, validation report 2 is due by 2028-06-15, and validation report 3 is due by 2028-12-15.
Your post-completion OPT filing window is from 2026-02-14 to 2026-06-14 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(B)(2)].
No, you are not currently over the post-completion OPT unemployment limit. You have used 45 of the 90 allowed days of unemployment, leaving 45 days remaining.

To be eligible for a 24-month STEM OPT extension, the degree that serves as the basis for the application must be in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics field and must be contained within a category on the STEM Designated Degree Program List [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(2)] and [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(2)(ii) and (iii)]. Therefore, a non-STEM economics degree would not make you eligible unless it qualifies and appears on that list.
You must report the loss of your employment to your DSO within 10 days of the change. Based on the computed findings, for the end of Beta on 2028-01-31, you must report it to the DSO by 2028-02-10.

You must file Form I-765 for post-completion OPT from 2026-09-19 to 2026-12-02, which is no later than 30 days after your program end date and within 30 days of the DSO recommendation [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(B)(2)].
You can file Form I-765 for post-completion OPT from 2026-05-16 to 2026-09-13 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(B)(2)].
The latest OPT start date you can request is 2027-01-17, as the requested OPT start date can be no later than this date [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(D)].

You must complete all post-completion practical training within a 14-month period following the completion of your study [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(A)(3)]. Given that your program ended on 2026-05-15, all post-completion OPT must be completed by 2027-07-15, unless you are exempt due to a STEM extension [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(A)(3)].

After your post-completion OPT ends on 2027-05-31, you are allowed an additional 30-day period to prepare for departure from the United States or to otherwise seek to maintain lawful status [8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v)]. This departure period ends on 2027-06-30 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v)].
Your 12-month self-evaluation (Form I-983) is due to the DSO by 2028-06-11 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(9)(i)].
Your STEM OPT extension period ends on 2029-05-31 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(iii)(A)].
Your new Form I-983 for your new job starting on 2028-03-01 is due to the DSO by 2028-03-11 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(7)(iv)].
You have used 59 of the 150 allowed days of unemployment during your OPT and STEM extension, leaving 91 days left [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E)].

No, you are not okay because you have exceeded the allowed days of unemployment. During post-completion OPT, you may not accrue an aggregate of more than 90 days of unemployment [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E)]. You have used 102 of the 90 allowed days of unemployment with 0 left [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E)]. Additionally, after OPT ends on 2027-05-31, the 30-day period to depart or change status ends on 2027-06-30 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(v)].
You must file Form I-765 for the 24-month STEM OPT extension from 2027-03-02 to 2027-05-31, and within 60 days of the DSO recommendation (by 2027-05-14).

During post-completion OPT, students may not accrue an aggregate of more than 90 days of unemployment. Students granted a 24-month OPT extension may not accrue an aggregate of more than 150 days of unemployment during a total OPT period, including the post-completion OPT period and any subsequent 24-month extension period [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E)].

An F-1 student can perform on-campus employment on the school's premises, which includes on-location commercial firms that provide services for students on campus (such as the school bookstore or cafeteria), or at an off-campus location that is educationally affiliated with the school [8 CFR 214.2(f)(9)(i)]. For off-campus locations, the educational affiliation must be associated with the school's established curriculum or related to contractually funded research projects at the post-graduate level, and the employment must be an integral part of the student's educational program [8 CFR 214.2(f)(9)(i)].

Curricular practical training (CPT) is defined as alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education, or any other type of required internship or practicum that is offered by sponsoring employers through cooperative agreements with the school, and which is an integral part of an established curriculum. An F-1 student may be authorized by the Designated School Official (DSO) to participate in CPT [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(i)].
While on STEM OPT, you must report a change of address to your DSO within 10 days of the change [8 CFR 214.2(f)(12)(ii)(A), 8 CFR 214.2(f)(17)].

Yes, you are required to report any interruption of your optional practical training employment to your DSO for the duration of the optional practical training [8 CFR 214.2(f)(12)(i)]. Additionally, you must report the loss of employment to your DSO within 10 days of the change [8 CFR 214.2(f)(12)(ii)(A)].

Yes, you can return to the United States to resume employment after a period of temporary absence if you have an unexpired EAD issued for post-completion practical training, are otherwise admissible, and use the EAD in combination with a Form I-20 endorsed for reentry by your DSO within the last six months [8 CFR 214.2(f)(13)(ii)].

A reduction in compensation not tied to a reduction in hours worked is considered a material change to or deviation from the training plan on Form I-983 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(9)(ii)]. Because of this, you and your employer must sign a modified Form I-983 reflecting this change [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(9)(ii)]. You and your employer must also ensure that this modified Form I-983 is submitted to your DSO at the earliest available opportunity [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(9)(ii)].

No, you may not begin optional practical training until the date indicated on your employment authorization document, Form I-766 [8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(A)]. You also may not begin OPT employment prior to the approved start date on your Employment Authorization Document, Form I-766 or successor form [8 CFR 214.2(f)(11)(i)(D)].
